title: October 27 — Slider3 and Antti's Instanton 2: lifted-wave observers against ordinary controls
summary: Two missing same-day paper-adjacent repositories. Slider3 moves from approximate coherent wave-contrast to a finite seven-coordinate positive conserved wave-current and directional planar solver; phase sensitivity matches ordinary delay-space and coherent-intensity controls. AnttisInstanton2 reproduces a free-wave lifted-current / fixed-fiber Dirichlet construction, tests 256 independent energy-matched waves, finds no held-out prediction advantage beyond L4, flux and phase controls, then instruments the nonlinear phi-four CoM against an approximate focus center with periodic reliability controls. The OpenAI theorem is not a theorem about nonlinear particle jumps or memory.

nodes.claim: Browser interference microscope comparing matched-power free waves, including coherent versus phase-scrambled conditions, followed by a mathematically traceable finite-wave 7×7 source current and direction-dependent planar Appendix D disk experiment based on the October 25 OpenAI local-smoothing paper.
nodes.survived: The finite-wave source-current positivity and seven-column divergence checks passed stated numerical tests (maximum residual 5.28e-6 at step 1e-3); the fixed-Q planar discrete equation reports a relative residual 5.08e-14. In 64/64 noiseless phase-change trials the current and planar potential change while Fourier powers remain unchanged (0/64).
nodes.killed: Ordinary coherent intensity and a three-delay scalar sensor also detect all 64/64 tested phase changes. The original isotropic auxiliary display can peak on six phase-scrambled waves (4.683) more strongly than two phase-locked ones (1.161) at equal displacement power, so a bright instantaneous peak is not evidence of stable coherence. No demonstrated information, accuracy, or cost advantage over phase-aware baselines; the two paper constructions use different finite mode sets and do not recreate the complete local-smoothing proof.
nodes.era: October 27: lifted-wave observers and field-defined centers

nodes.claim: Preserves Antti's nonlinear phi-four substrate with a green center of positive field, adds exact imaginary-ray free-wave calibration, a free-wave positive conserved lifted tensor and true Proposition 2.2 time density driving a fixed-Phi variable-coefficient Appendix D disk, and compares field/focus centroids through time.
nodes.survived: Source-reported numerical current positivity, divergence and complex-chart pushforward checks pass; a 256-independent-wave frozen split (166 training/90 test, identical Fourier powers and physical energy) and headless tests reproduce a fair ordinary-versus-paper predictive comparison. The newest live observer saves both periodic center motions, their signed separation, lag curves and ordinary gradient/kinetic controls; 30 tests passed at merge.
nodes.killed: Paper-derived fixed-Phi slice response correlates 0.999714 with ordinary present L4 across the 256 equal-power waves. Future log-L4 RMSE is 0.040245 for ordinary L4/flux/phase controls and 0.040435 with the auxiliary response; paired CI crosses zero. No held-out predictive benefit established; live nonlinear lead/lag observation is exploratory rather than proof of causation, a transported particle or a conserved nonlinear current. The full fiber/two-circle theorem is not implemented.
nodes.era: October 27: lifted-wave observers and field-defined centers

edges.why: Both explicitly test ideas drawn from the October 25 OpenAI wave paper. Sihti compares directional image windows; Slider3 instead implements a finite coherent current and auxiliary inverse, with conventional phase-delay controls. Independent mechanisms, not a code fork or evidence that the paper improves either.

Same-day independent implementations of the paper's conserved lifted wave-current and planar Dirichlet geometry meet at the question of interference-sensitive diagnostics versus ordinary observables. Instanton2 adds an unchanged nonlinear phi-four field and held-out prediction testing; conceptual convergence, not inherited source code.

motifs.title: A conserved interference current is mathematically richer, not automatically a better detector
motifs.description: Slider3 shows relative phases affect the paper current and planar disk but also ordinary coherent amplitude and delayed measurements. AnttisInstanton2 obtains nearly the same prediction from ordinary L4/flux/phase summaries as from adding its fixed-fiber auxiliary response. Preserve proof-specific mathematics without claiming new information inaccessible to fair, phase-aware baselines.

motifs.title: An instantaneous bright focus is neither memory nor a persistent particle
motifs.description: Slider3's six phase-scrambled waves can make a higher instantaneous potential peak without stable temporal coherence; AnttisInstanton2's green positive-field CoM and auxiliary focus CoM can separate or coincide as their field distributions reorganize. A global center may lie in a dark region and may become undefined when diffuse. Only future held-out center-motion controls can test a lead–lag claim.
